script.title: The 'boss' who emails HR for every W-2, played out
script.hook: 1 email from the 'CEO' to payroll can hand every employee's W-2 to a tax thief.

segments.heading: Hook
segments.narration: One email to payroll from the CEO can hand every employee's W-2 to a tax thief. Here's how it reads.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. Dhruv on camera holding a phone No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The email
segments.narration: Hi, quick favour. I need copies of all employee W-2s for a meeting with the accountant. PDF is fine. I'm traveling, so email is best. Thanks.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. an email on a phone screen No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Pause
segments.narration: Pause. If this landed in your inbox at work, what would you do first?
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. a full-screen countdown card reading PAUSE No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The tells
segments.narration: The sender's address is one letter off, or a personal email. The request is urgent and unusual. And the boss can't be reached, so you can't check. And it wants PDFs by email, the least safe way to send them.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. an email address with one letter circled No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Why it matters
segments.narration: W-2s hold names, Social Security numbers and wages. That's everything a thief needs to file fake returns for your whole company, before your coworkers file their own.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. a stack of W-2s blowing away No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The rule
segments.narration: One call. Before sending any W-2s, call the person who asked, on a number you already have. Not the number in the email. Payroll teams can make it a written rule: W-2s never go out by email. If it was already sent, tell your manager and the IRS right away.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. the small round teal shield mascot with big curious eyes holding a phone No text, no logos, no real people.

script.title: 'Dependent already claimed': your child's SSN, what now?
script.hook: 1 rejection message, 'dependent already claimed', can mean someone used your child's SSN.

segments.heading: Hook
segments.narration: One rejection message: dependent already claimed. It can mean someone used your child's Social Security number. Here's what to do.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. the small round teal shield mascot with big curious eyes holding a rejected form No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Two causes
segments.narration: Sometimes it's a mix-up: an ex, a grandparent or another relative claimed the same child. Sometimes it's a stranger who bought or stole the number. Either way, the e-filed return won't go through until it's sorted.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. two paths from one form No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Pause
segments.narration: Pause. Before you panic, who else could have claimed your child this year? Think about it.
segments.on_screen_text: Pause: who else could it be?
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. a full-screen countdown card reading PAUSE No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: If it's family
segments.narration: Talk to them first. Only one person can claim a child, and the IRS has tie-breaker rules. If you're the one entitled to claim, you can file on paper and the IRS will sort it out by mail.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. two adults talking with a form No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: If it's a stranger
segments.narration: If nobody you know claimed them, treat it as identity theft. Follow the IRS identity theft steps, and file on paper with your correct information.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. a shield with a child icon No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Next year
segments.narration: Then lock it. A dependent can have their own IP PIN, and an e-filed return claiming them is rejected without it. Get one for each child in January. It's free, and a new one comes every year, just like yours.
segments.on_screen_text: Get your child an IP PIN
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. a 6-digit code on a small shield No text, no logos, no real people.

script.title: IRS letter or fake? 3 checks before you call
script.hook: 3 checks tell you if an IRS letter is real, 5 days before Tax Day.

segments.heading: Hook
segments.narration: Three checks tell you if an IRS letter is real. Tax Day is in five days, so scammers are mailing too.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. a letter on a kitchen table No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Pause
segments.narration: Pause. This letter says you owe four thousand dollars and must call within ten days. What would you check first?
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. a full-screen countdown card reading PAUSE No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Check 1
segments.narration: One: the notice number, usually CP or LTR and a number, in the corner. Look it up on I R S dot gov to see what that notice is really about. If the number doesn't match a real notice, that's your answer.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. a corner of a letter, number circled No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Check 2
segments.narration: Two: sign in to your IRS online account. If you really owe, the balance is there. If there's no balance, don't pay the letter.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. a laptop with the account page No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: Check 3
segments.narration: Three: if you need to call, use the number on I R S dot gov, not the one in the letter. Fake letters copy everything except the phone number.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. two phone numbers, one crossed out No text, no logos, no real people.

segments.heading: The payment
segments.narration: And the real IRS takes payment through I R S dot gov or a check to the U.S. Treasury. Never gift cards, crypto or a payment app to a person. Already paid? Call your bank right away and report it at report fraud dot F T C dot gov.
segments.visual_prompt: Clean flat vector illustration, deep navy and cream with teal and amber warning accents, simple shapes. the small round teal shield mascot with big curious eyes with a check No text, no logos, no real people.
